recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not duplicate the THO LOINC case-sensitivity paragraph in FHIR core unless Vocabulary/TSMG later reverses the external-code-system guidance migration.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive FHIR-core ValueSet issue asking for a note clarifying whether LOINC filter values such as SCALE_TYP=DOC are case sensitive; Jira comments recorded confirmation that LOINC is not case sensitive.
initial_application: Applied by git-svn commit b91df9d9ee0dc9afb102e2b3df25893c4cbd1743 / svn revision 4490, which added a Case Sensitivity section to the then-current source/loinc.html page.
additional_context: FHIR-35933 and UP-289 later moved the external code system usage pages from FHIR core to HL7 Terminology. The current build-scoped source/terminologies-systems.html page links LOINC to THO, the current THO LOINC page contains the case-sensitivity guidance, and current SCALE_TYP filters use LOINC part-code values rather than the old uppercase DOC string.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No core source edit is needed because the requested clarification was historically applied and the current authoritative guidance is maintained in THO with a core link to it.

related_jiras.note: Moved the core Using X with FHIR pages, including LOINC, to THO and replaced local core content with links.
Implemented the THO-side migration of external code system usage pages.
Later DSTU1 issue about changing a concrete SCALE_TYP=DOC filter to the LOINC-cased value; current source now uses LOINC part-code filters instead.
